newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S. Paris envoy Harriman in serious condition.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Paris envoy Harriman in serious condition.

text.p: U.S. ambassador to France Pamela Harriman was in serious condition in the American Hospital of Paris on Tuesday after suffering a brain haemorrhage on Monday evening, the U.S. embassy said.

Harriman, 76, a close supporter of President Bill Clinton, was taken ill at the Ritz Hotel where she had gone for a swim. "The initial diagonisis is that the Ambassador suffered a cerebral haemorrhage. She remains in serious condition," an embassy statement said.
A haemorrhage can cause paralysis or death by blocking the blood supply to the brain.
The statement said members of Harriman's family were at her side at the hospital in the suburb of Neuilly, west of Paris.
Her son, Winston Churchill, a British member of parliament and grandchild of the wartime British prime minister, was at her bedside, the State Department said.
A senior U.S. official in Washington, speaking on condition of anonymity, said: "I understand she's very, very ill."
